subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: What core recovery policy should OpenClaw use when a subagent stops making tool-call progress while its parent/channel session is blocked?
rationale: The useful behavior is clear, but choosing default-on versus opt-in thresholds, per-spawn overrides, kill semantics, and user-visible channel recovery can change existing long-running subagent workflows and persisted config contracts.

options.title: Design core nudge/kill policy first
options.body: Approve a small product/API design for the activity signal, defaults, config names, parent notification, and upgrade behavior before queuing implementation.

options.title: Block on session activity API
options.body: Make this issue wait for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39127 and implement escalation only after gateway-owned activity state exists.

options.title: Keep to manual recovery only
options.body: Do not add automatic stall kills yet; focus instead on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87445 for explicit operator-controlled kill/reap actions.

recommendation.title: Design core nudge/kill policy first
recommendation.body: Approve a small product/API design for the activity signal, defaults, config names, parent notification, and upgrade behavior before queuing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent history on subagent timeout enforcement and merged the closest current-main recovery work.
